articles.title: Designing a skill
articles.description: Agent skills can be treated like apps whose interfaces happen to be written largely through instructions, with both the human invoking the skill and the AI interpreting it acting as users. Building a polished skill requires many familiar design practices, including finding the right form, refining copy, creating a visual system, anticipating repeated use, offering meaningful customization, and testing across different contexts. Precise instructions matter because agents fall back on familiar patterns when given vague directions, making skills a useful place to encode the context, trade-offs, intuition, and taste that individual prompts cannot reliably communicate.
articles.one-liner: Designing AI agent skills requires the same rigor as traditional app development, focusing on precise instructions, user-facing surfaces, and robust stress testing.

summary.what: Noman (iamnoman.com) argues that skills are the 'apps' of the agentic era, requiring developers to move beyond vague prompts toward structured, intent-based design patterns.
summary.why: This indicates a shift where the quality of AI output is determined by the developer's ability to encode domain-specific context and constraints into structured instructions (skills) rather than relying on LLM generalization.
summary.takeaway: Try the 'npx skills add nomanjack/interface-bts' command to see how complex interface logic can be packaged as an executable agent skill.

articles.deep-summary:
* **Agent as User**: Design skills by considering both the human end-user and the AI agent as distinct users with different interface needs.
* **Instruction Precision**: Avoid subjective adjectives like 'clean' or 'minimal'; replace them with specific stylistic constraints and token-based design systems.
* **Configuration**: Provide mechanisms for users to customize agent output to prevent 'one-size-fits-all' results.
* **Testing**: Treat agent skills as software; test them across various projects and scenarios to identify failure modes before final deployment.
articles.decoder:
* **Agentic Era**: A period where AI systems are tasked with performing autonomous actions, rather than just generating text or images.
* **Tokens**: In this context, standardized variables for design parameters like typography, color palettes, and spacing.

articles.title: You Are the Best Artist
articles.description: Art is less about conveying emotion to an audience than about capturing it, since a painter alone in a studio still makes art. Comparing skills with others can help, but becoming a better artist is personal, because nobody can express someone's feelings like they can.
articles.one-liner: Art is a personal act of capturing emotion for one's own fulfillment rather than a service intended to satisfy an external audience.

summary.what: Koos Looijesteijn explores the distinction between creative work performed for professional compensation and creative work produced for self-expression.

articles.title: Bioluminescent Alien Worlds That Will Make You Want to Pack Your Bags for the Cosmos
articles.description: Vancouver-based 3D artist Calder Moore builds bioluminescent forests, glowing flora, towering monoliths, and surreal planetary systems under twilight or starry skies.
articles.one-liner: Calder Moore utilizes advanced 3D rendering and particle systems to create hyper-detailed, bioluminescent alien environments.

summary.what: Vancouver-based artist Calder Moore showcases digital landscapes that blend organic wilderness with complex geometric architecture, using professional VFX techniques.

articles.decoder: * **VFX**: Visual effects; the process by which imagery is created or manipulated outside the context of a live-action shot in filmmaking.

articles.title: This 3D Artist Achieves Incredible Realism to Breathe Life into Striking Character Designs
articles.description: A smug goblin, an albino demon, an adolescent chimp, and a dark elf showcase the striking realism of Australian 3D artist Tom Newbury.
articles.one-liner: Australian 3D artist Tom Newbury showcases his workflow for achieving hyper-realistic character designs using a combination of industry-standard modeling tools.

summary.what: Tom Newbury, a veteran 3D artist with 15 years of commercial experience, details how he uses software including Maya, ZBrush, Mari, Marvelous Designer, and Blender to create realistic character models. His portfolio includes stylized figures like a smug goblin and a realistic chimpanzee influenced by Weta's work on the Planet of the Apes films.

articles.deep-summary:
* Newbury utilizes a multi-tool pipeline to balance technical detail with artistic intent.
* The workflow focuses on translating 2D concepts into 3D, often inspired by existing illustration or cinematic character design.
* Key tools mentioned: ZBrush (sculpting), Maya (modeling/layout), Mari (texturing), and Marvelous Designer (cloth simulation).
articles.decoder:
* **ZBrush**: A digital sculpting tool used for creating high-resolution models with intricate details.
* **Mari**: A 3D painting software used for creating high-fidelity textures on complex 3D models.
